pride_data.title: TRAIP regulates DNA double-strand break-induced ATM activation
pride_data.projectDescription: TRAIP is a functional E3 ubiquitin ligase with a RING finger domain at the N-terminal end.  To find TRAIP partners and substrates we used a proximity-dependent biotinylation assay (Bio-ID) which can identify direct protein-protein interaction but also proteins building a complex without requiring direct interactions.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: We used a proximity-dependent biotin labeling system (Bio-ID). TRAIP was fused to the N-terminal end of the promiscuous prokaryotic biotin protein ligase BirAR118G (BirA*) which was tagged with a HA sequence (TRAIP-BirA*-HA).  The BirA* part of the fusion protein provided a biotinylase activity allowing to mark proteins interacting either directly with TRAIP or found in its proximity  After labelling, biotinylated proteins were purified by streptavidin affinity and separated by 1D gel electrophoresis before in-gel digestion with trypsin.  MS analyses were performed on a LTQ-Velos Pro orbitrap mass spectrometer (Thermo Fisher Scientific, Bremen, Germany) interfaced to a nanocapillary HPLC (Dionex RSLC3000) equipped with a 75um ID, 25cm C18 reversed-phase column.  Peptides were separated along a 95 min gradient from 5% to 45% Acetonitrile in 0.1% formic acid at 0.3 ul/min.  Full MS survey scans were performed at 60’000 resolution. In data-dependent acquisition controlled by Xcalibur 2.2 software (Thermo Fisher), the twenty most intense multiply charged precursor ions detected in the full MS survey scan were selected for collision-induced dissociation and analysis in the linear trap with an isolation window of 4.0 m/z and then dynamically excluded from further selection during 25s.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: Collections of tandem mass spectra for database searching were generated from raw data and searched using Mascot (Matrix Science, London, UK; version 2.5.0) against the release 2014_08 of the UNIPROT database, (SWISSPROT + TrEMBL, www.uniprot.org) restricted to human taxonomy.  The software Scaffold 4.3.3 (Proteome Software Inc.) was used to validate MS/MS based peptide (minimum 90% probability by the Scaffold Local FDR algorithm) and protein (min 95% probability by the Protein Prophet algorithm [40]) identifications, perform dataset alignment and subtraction as well as parsimony analysis to discriminate homologous hits.
